sourcePipeline.meaning: Pinned upstream sync stage fetches preview, upcoming-change, and schema inputs, then writes generated static data for each GraphQL version.

Pinned upstream processSchemas parses the complete GraphQL schema, prefers explicit @docsCategory metadata, derives mutation-input and Connection/Edge/reference categories from their semantic sources, and keeps ambiguous ownership unresolved instead of guessing.

Pinned upstream sync stage materializes already categorized schema data into per-category schema fragments and category-map.json; category ownership is resolved upstream by semantic-category-resolution.
Pinned upstream loader reads schema fragments by GraphQL version and category; this benchmark preserves that version/category provenance instead of flattening it into product authority.
Pinned upstream validator defines the generated schema member shape for queries, mutations, objects, interfaces, enums, unions, input objects, and scalars.

nodes.meaning: A human account/actor surface used as a participant, member, assignee, owner, or project owner.
A top-level governance scope that relates organizations, members, and enterprise teams.
A team owned by an enterprise scope and assignable to organizations.
A governance and membership scope that owns teams and repositories and can own projects.
An organization-scoped team with members, hierarchy, repositories, and linked projects.
A resource container with an owner, lifecycle, access relationships, work items, labels, milestones, discussions, and linked projects; Git/SCM fields are excluded from this projection.

A planning and management entity that can link repositories and teams and own project items, field configurations, status updates, and read views. FPT workflows and iterations remain deferred until a real general-management consumer requires them.
An item participating in a project planning surface; its content remains a referenced resource rather than a second authority.
A repository-scoped work/collaboration item with assignment, labels, milestone, hierarchy, dependency, state, and project relationships; this is a neutral projection of Issue semantics.
A reusable classification resource for repository-scoped work and discussions.
A repository-scoped goal/target that groups work items.
A repository-scoped conversation with category, comments, answer semantics, labels, and lifecycle.
A repository-scoped classification for discussions.
A comment belonging to a discussion and optionally serving as its accepted answer.
A user-scoped collection of observable contribution facts over a time range; it aggregates facts without owning the underlying resources.
An observable fact that a user created a repository, carrying actor, repository context, and occurrence time.
An observable fact that a user joined the platform, carrying actor and occurrence time.
The FPT Contribution interface: an observable contribution made by a user with restriction state, occurrence time, locator, and actor; concrete contribution facts provide real variation.
An observable fact that a user created a repository-scoped work item; this is a neutral projection of CreatedIssueContribution.
A pending intent for a user to become an enterprise member; pending intent is not active membership.
A pending intent for a user to join an organization, including the pending organization role.
A pending intent for a user to gain repository access, including the permission proposed by the invitation.
A timestamped user interaction applied to reactable collaboration content; it is an interaction signal, not approval or authorization.
A comment belonging to a repository-scoped work item; this is the neutral projection of IssueComment.
An organization-defined work-item type with its own identity and lifecycle metadata; it is distinct from labels, status, and milestones.
A Project-owned field configuration used for planning metadata without becoming a second authority for underlying work truth.
A Project-owned status update record with its own status and planning dates.

referenceContracts.meaning: FPT models starring as an activity contract over Starrable resources; this is reference evidence for an interaction signal, not product adoption.
FPT models watch/notification subscription as an activity contract over Subscribable resources; this is reference evidence for notification-interest semantics only.
FPT Node identity supplies a stable opaque ID contract for cross-resource references.
FPT UniformResourceLocatable separates URL/resourcePath locator evidence from owner identity and product routing decisions.
FPT search is a cross-resource, authorization-filtered projection with its own result connection, not a resource owner.
FPT connection-style pagination evidence is referenced as result traversal behavior, not domain ownership.

derivedResults.meaning: A profile recognition derived from qualifying events/actions. Public FPT exposes observable contribution/activity facts but does not expose AchievementDefinition, qualification rules, grant state, or progress as GraphQL types.

observableModel.note: The FPT Contribution contract and listed concrete facts demonstrate observable fact/actor/context/time primitives. RepositoryContribution has direct Repository context; WorkItemContribution targets WorkItem, whose Repository context remains owned by WorkItem. Public sources do not state that every listed fact qualifies for an Achievement.

evidencePolicy.graphqlFpt: Nodes, edges, projections, observable fact collections, event facts, actor/context relationships, and temporal fields must be traceable to the pinned src/graphql/data/fpt revision.
evidencePolicy.canonicalDocsSupplement: A derived result may cite pinned canonical github/docs content when GitHub documents the product semantic but FPT does not expose the result as a GraphQL type.
evidencePolicy.boundary: Canonical-doc supplementation may explain a derived result such as Achievement; it must not invent unexposed definition, qualification, grant, progress, storage, or runtime semantics.
evidencePolicy.graphSemantics: FPT interfaces may appear as fact contracts only when current FPT exposes real implementing types. Edge attributes preserve relationship-specific role/permission semantics without creating duplicate Role or Permission owners.
evidencePolicy.relationshipIntent: Invitation nodes represent pending relationship intent only; pending role/permission must not be treated as active membership or authorization.
evidencePolicy.cardinality: Graph edges express a supported semantic relationship, not GraphQL non-nullability or cardinality. The pinned source field remains authoritative for optionality and multiplicity.

supplementalEvidence.purpose: Documented derived profile recognition semantics that are not exposed as Achievement GraphQL result types in FPT.
